approachQuestion.prompt:
Independent rosters. A read-only array contains b rosters, each an array of signed 64-bit IDs. Return one boolean per roster: true exactly when that roster has no repeated ID. The same ID may occur in different rosters without invalidating either. There are 1 <= b <= 100,000 rosters, N <= 200,000 total entries, and each roster length is directly available. Let K be the largest roster length, possibly zero. Choose minimum expected total time, then peak auxiliary storage under this model: a hash set of d fixed-size keys supports expected amortized constant-cost membership/insertion and peak storage proportional to d+1, including resizing. Allocate and release sets per roster; releasing d keys costs at most proportional to d+1. Expectations concern hashing, not the input distribution. The b booleans are required output.

Example 1: Input: rosters=[[4,8],[4,4],[],[8]]. Output: [true,false,true,true].
Example 2: Input: rosters=[[],[]]. Output: [true,true].

options.text: For each roster, create a fresh empty set and a true flag. Check every ID, mark false on a repeated key, and insert it; write the flag, then release the set before the next roster.
options.feedback: Uniqueness is local to one roster. Once its flag is written, its keys can no longer affect another answer and can be released.

options.text: Create a separate set per roster, check uniqueness within each, and retain every set until the full output has been returned.
options.feedback: All booleans are correct, but sets from completed rosters are unnecessary. Retaining them can make peak storage depend on the whole collection rather than the largest roster.

options.text: Use one set for all rosters without clearing it, marking a roster false whenever its ID was seen anywhere before.
options.feedback: For [[4],[4]], both rosters are locally unique and should return [true,true]. The global set wrongly marks the second false.

options.text: Mark a roster false only when two adjacent IDs match.
options.feedback: Input rosters are not sorted. Roster [4,8,4] repeats 4 but has no adjacent equal IDs, so this incorrectly returns true.

feedback.reason: Peak memory measures simultaneously live state; independent batches allow completed state to be released.
details: Process rosters sequentially. Create a new hash set, scan the entire current roster, and insert every ID while recording whether membership ever reports a repeat. Write its boolean into the result and release the set before moving to the next roster. Do not retain completed sets or copies of their keys.

An ID repeated across two different rosters is legal; only repetition inside one roster matters. Release the first roster's set before creating the next. Total work follows all N entries, but peak memory follows the largest current roster K, not the sum of completed rosters.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For release-set-per-roster, choose expected total time and peak auxiliary space in terms of b rosters, N total entries, and K maximum roster length. Include empty rosters, set creation/release and resizing. Exclude the b required output booleans and read-only inputs; no recursion is used.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard bound for the complete execution. Count peak simultaneously live auxiliary storage; exclude supplied input and required output.
Word arithmetic, indexing, and copying one fixed-size element take constant time. No hashing or recursion is used.

options.text: Expected O(b + N) time, O(K + 1) auxiliary space
Expected O(b + N) time, O(b + N) auxiliary space
Expected O(K + 1) time, O(K + 1) auxiliary space
Expected O(b + N) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Scan b roster headers and N entries while retaining only one roster's set.
details: Each roster contributes constant setup/release work plus expected work proportional to its entries, summing to O(b+N). Only the current roster’s set is live, with at most K keys; O(K+1) handles all-empty input too. A roster with K distinct keys realizes this peak. Retaining every completed set would accumulate storage, but this method releases them.
“Expected O(b + N) time, O(b + N) auxiliary space”: This counts released sets as live. Peak current-set storage is controlled by K, not the total entries across rosters.
“Expected O(K + 1) time, O(K + 1) auxiliary space”: The largest roster controls peak space, but every roster and entry is processed for total time.
“Expected O(b + N) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: When a roster has K distinct IDs, the current set stores all K of them.
